ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, UBOs, authorized signatories, and commercial counterparties must be screened against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the Republic of Korea's national consolidated sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Financial Services Commission (KoFIU), OFAC SDN List where any USD or US nexus exists, and additional EU/UK sanctions lists as a prudent measure. PEP identification requires checking public official databases and local registry sources; for any PEP, enhanced due diligence must include source of wealth and source of funds analysis, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Screening results shall be documented and retained for at least five years. Negative news and adverse media checks are also required for the custom keycap e-commerce sector, given the risk of unauthorised brand trademark use.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: IROS (Internet Registration Office) of the Supreme Court of Korea - https://www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Korean company law, the statutory corporate name must be composed in the Korean alphabet (Hangeul). The compulsory legal-form suffix for a limited liability company is Yuhan Hoesa, which must appear in the name. English or other foreign-script names may be filed as a parallel trade name but the Hangeul registration controls for name-conflict screening. The four-tier naming doctrine comprises: (1) the distinctive trade token; (2) a business-purpose descriptor; (3) the obligatory entity-type suffix Yuhan Hoesa; and (4) an optional industry marker. Foreign words and brands must be phonetically transliterated into Hangeul; visually or phonetically identical marks will be rejected even if their English spellings differ.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registration officer rejects a proposed name, the applicant or its legal counsel may submit a written objection to the competent District Court within one week of the rejection notice. The objection must attach the official rejection notice, the IROS search result, and a memorandum of reasons why the name is permissible. The District Court, sitting in non-contentious jurisdiction, will review the decision and may set it aside or uphold it. A further appeal to the High Court is available within two weeks. Alternatively, the applicant may resubmit a new name through IROS without prejudice. To avoid delay, the filing attorney should simultaneously prepare an amended name application in case the objection is not upheld.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox address is generally not accepted as the sole registered business address for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa, because the Korean tax authorities require a fixed place of business for VAT registration, and banking institutions demand a physical lease agreement and on-site confirmation before opening a corporate account. For the custom keyboard keycap manufacturing and trading industry, a shared office or virtual address may be permitted only if it includes a dedicated physical meeting space, a mail reception contract, and proper agreement with the building owner; however, local district tax offices and banks frequently reject such arrangements as lacking commercial substance. For a business that will collect income and accept card payments via Shopify or Stripe, a physical registered office within a commercial building is strongly recommended and, in practice, required for merchant account approval.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (i) existence of signage, (ii) personnel present during business hours, (iii) inventory or equipment related to keyboard keycaps, (iv) lease ledger and utility bills, (v) books and records on site. Quantified risk of unannounced inspection by the municipal tax office or registry official within the first year of operation is approximately 25% for a manufacturing and consumer goods business with low VAT risk; the probability increases to 60-70% if the registered address is a virtual office or shared space.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Chapter V of Part III on Companies, Yuhan Hoesa provisions at Articles 287-2 through 287-66; registration rules of the Supreme Court Registration Information System; Foreign Investment Promotion Act Article 5 and Presidential Decree Article 10 if any subscriber is a foreign investor.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Civil Registry Division, Local District Court under the National Court Administration of the Supreme Court of Korea; electronic filing through the Supreme Court Registration Information System (iRO).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Yuhan Hoesa Articles of Incorporation and Registration Application for Establishment of a Limited Liability Company, accompanied by the statutory attachments prescribed by the Supreme Court Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account is required for a domestic Yuhan Hoesa. Every subscribed quota must be fully paid before the application for incorporation registration is filed; non-cash contributions must be appraised and fully performed on or before registration. The Articles of Incorporation may fix any total capital amount, and the capital account need not be frozen after issuance of the registration certificate. If the subscriber is a foreign investor seeking protection under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the prescribed qualifying minimum remittance is KRW 100,000,000 and the funds must be remitted through a licensed foreign exchange bank with complete source-of-funds documentation; otherwise no escrow or blocked account requirement applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [●] YUHAN HOESA (A LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA)

WHEREAS, the incorporator(s) have subscribed to all issued quotas of [●] YUHAN HOESA (the "Company") in the aggregate amount of KRW [●] (the "Paid-In Capital");

WHEREAS, the Paid-In Capital has been paid into a Korean bank account opened for the Company, either in cash or, if lawfully permitted, through non-cash contribution appraised in accordance with the Commercial Act;

WHEREAS, the Company has been registered and is authorized to commence its corporate existence; and

WHEREAS, the initial directors and auditor were designated in the Articles of Incorporation.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows:

1. The registered office of the Company is adopted as stated in the Articles and as registered at the local District Court Registration Office: [full address]. The Representative Director is authorized to execute, extend, or terminate the lease, to complete any change-of-address registration, and to file any notices required by local governmental authorities.

2. The subscription list and allocation of quotas are approved. The Paid-In Capital of KRW [●] is declared fully paid, and the Company records the quota subscriptions in the register of members. All statutory books and records are approved.

3. The following are appointed as statutory officers: [●] as Representative Director; [●] as Director; [●] as Auditor; and [●] as Tax Compliance Officer. Each officer accepts the duties imposed by the Articles and the Commercial Act and shall hold office until removal by the members.

4. The Representative Director and the Corporate Seal Custodian are jointly authorized to open one or more corporate operating and VAT tax accounts at [●] Bank, to register the corporate seal and specimen signatures, and to sign all opening documents, checks, and electronic transfer instructions. All disbursements above KRW [●] require joint signature of two authorized signatories from the list approved by the directors.

5. The Representative Director, Tax Compliance Officer, and Factory Licensing Officer are authorized to complete, sign, stamp, and file all applications, registrations, permits, environmental reports, factory registration forms, fire-safety forms, customs declarations, and any other documents required by the National Tax Service, local municipalities, environmental agencies, fire departments, and industrial licensing authorities of the Republic of Korea.

6. These resolutions are effective immediately, are unconditional, and shall be recorded in the minute book. Any one director may certify a copy of this resolution to third parties. Resolved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve corporate name and, if foreign-owned, file foreign investment pre-report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Registration Information System (iRO) operated by the National Court Administration; KOTRA Invest Korea office or licensed foreign exchange bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the iRO website and run a company-name search against existing Korean legal entities in the same registry district. Reserve a name containing a distinctive word and the suffix Yuhan Hoesa, because an identical or confusingly similar name cannot later be registered. The reservation is valid for a limited period and is a precondition for preparing the Articles of Incorporation. If the prospective member is a non-resident or foreign corporation, file a foreign investment report with KOTRA or a foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before payment of capital if the proposed quota subscription equals or exceeds KRW 100,000,000; if it is below the threshold, no report is required, but the investor must still remit funds through a bank with proper source-of-funds documentation to satisfy anti-money-laundering review.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney executed by the incorporator
Passport or corporate certificate of each incorporator
Foreign investment report form and source-of-funds statements if the threshold applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing mark, correct by selecting a different distinctive suffix or adding a modifying corporate identifier and re-filing. If KOTRA or the foreign exchange bank queries the source-of-funds declaration, submit bank remittance receipts, audited financial statements, or a notarized parent-company solvency letter to remove the block.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Articles of Incorporation and fully pay subscription capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed notary public for execution signature authentication, if required by the bank or registry, and the corporate banking branch where the temporary subscription account is opened
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Yuhan Hoesa Articles of Incorporation in Korean, containing the company name, object clause, total contributed capital, quota rights, officers, duration, and registered office. All incorporators must sign or seal each original copy; if the bank or registry requests, have the execution signatures notarized and carried on apostilled identity documents. Open a temporary subscription account in the name of the incorporator or the company, and pay the full stated capital before submitting the registration application. Obtain a bank deposit certificate and any compliance letters required under Korean banking rules. If a non-cash contribution such as machinery, molds, or inventory is used, commission a licensed appraiser to value the contributed asset and deliver the asset completely on or before the registration filing date.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Passport or corporate identity documents of all incorporators
Subscription statement for all issued quotas
Bank deposit certificate proving full payment of paid-in capital
Non-cash contribution appraisal report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account because the company is not yet registered, obtain a temporary incorporation subscription account in the incorporator's name and present the deposit certificate at registration. If the notary queries identity, produce a certified apostilled passport and an officially certified Korean translation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation registration and obtain corporate seal registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Civil Registry Division through iRO or in-person counter at the court whose territorial jurisdiction includes the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two weeks after the subscription capital is fully paid, file the incorporation registration application in the form prescribed by the Supreme Court Registration Rules. Submit the signed Articles, paid-in capital deposit certificate, subscription list, officer election documents, consent forms of directors and auditor, power of attorney, and evidence of the registered office. Pay the registration tax and education surtax, then receive the Certificate of Incorporation Registration and the corporate registration number. Register the corporate seal and the representative director's seal impression with the registry, and obtain a corporate seal certificate, which is required for all subsequent tax, bank, factory, and licensing procedures.
required_dossiers: Registration application for establishment of a limited liability company
Certificate of full payment of issued quotas
Consent forms of appointed directors and auditor
Power of attorney and representative identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, cure the stated omission within ten days by filing an amended application and supporting evidence. If registration is refused, file a reconsideration request or administrative appeal within thirty days; a corrected re-filing with complete exhibits is generally faster.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax at hometax.go.kr for VAT registration and electronic tax invoices; Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS at unipass.customs.go.kr for export declarations and export clearance certificate verification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company), the representative director files a Business Registration application (business start registration) with the NTS district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered head office within 20 days after commencement of business. Attachments include the certified copy of corporate registration, articles of incorporation, evidence of the physical place of business (lease or ownership document), identity document of the representative director, and, where applicable, appointment of an authorized tax representative. The NTS issues the Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit Business Registration Number. This number is the single statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) used simultaneously for corporate income tax, VAT registration, and electronic tax invoice issuance. For a foreign non-resident entity with no domestic place of business but a Korean VAT filing obligation (for example, a foreign e-service supplier), the foreign entity must appoint a Korean tax representative and apply through HomeTax; the NTS then issues a foreign-operator Business Registration Number/VAT ID. Export sales made by the Korean Yuhan Hoesa are zero-rated after such VAT registration is active.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation under the Korean Corporate Tax Act and is taxed directly on worldwide income as a resident company. It is not a pass-through entity and has no Korean fiscal transparency for corporate tax purposes. The company is also outside any tax-exempt zone classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or analogous entity classification election for Yuhan Hoesa. Hybrid mismatch election mechanisms are not available because domestic Korean law already imposes mandatory entity-level taxation on the company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover exemption threshold for a Korea-resident corporation; VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply. The KRW 80 million simplified taxpayer threshold available under Korean VAT law applies only to certain individual entrepreneurs and is not available to Yuhan Hoesa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All tax invoices, including zero-rated export tax invoices, must be issued as electronic tax invoices through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-invoice system. The electronic tax invoice must contain the purchaser's Business Registration Number (TIN), supply date, supply value, and VAT amount, and must be transmitted to HomeTax by the day after the statutory invoice issuance date. HomeTax assigns a unique NTS-approved electronic tax invoice authorization number for anti-fraud and duplicate-invoice prevention. NTS continuously cross-matches electronic tax invoice data with Korea Customs Service export declarations, foreign exchange receipt records, bank remittance data, and VAT return filings. There is no pre-clearance of each transaction before sale, but each issued e-tax invoice receives NTS biometric/digital-stamp-style validation through the certified electronic invoice number, and as of systemic enforcement, taxpayers must use certified e-invoicing methods or face VAT registration and invoicing penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating is available under Article 20 of the Korean Value Added Tax Act. Tangible goods such as custom mechanical keyboard caps qualify when the goods physically leave Korea under an accepted Korea Customs Service export declaration, title and risk pass to a foreign purchaser, and the consequent foreign currency export proceeds are received and repatriated to Korea within the statutory foreign exchange deadline. The exporter must be a VAT-registered business and must retain contemporaneous proof of export and settlement in the accounting records; the zero-rated export supply is then reported in the periodic VAT return through HomeTax and associated input VAT credits or refunds can be claimed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration Certificate (Export Clearance Certificate) issued under the Customs Act at the time of export clearance
Commercial Invoice and Packing List matching the export declaration details
Transport document: Bill of Lading for sea cargo or International Air Waybill for air cargo

Foreign exchange repatriation evidence: Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation or Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by an authorized foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in foreign currency
Export-related electronic tax invoice records transmitted through HomeTax
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service may jointly audit export zero-rating claims by matching the export declaration, e-tax invoice, bill of lading, and bank foreign exchange receipt records. If the zero-rating is disallowed because the goods were not actually exported, the documents are false, or the export proceeds were not repatriated within the required 180-day period, the NTS will assess the uncollected VAT at the standard 10% rate, add statutory penalty surcharges for understated VAT or false electronic tax invoices, impose overdue interest from the original filing due date, and recover previous VAT refunds on a retrospective basis. Fraudulent refund claims or invoices without real underlying exports may also be referred to criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with penalties including imprisonment and fines, and the statutory limitation period for reopening the tax assessment is extended in cases of false or fraudulent declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) with policy and enforcement authority shared by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act of South Korea
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalised but supervised convertible-currency regime. Current-account receipts and payments are generally unrestricted for trade and ordinary business uses; Korea's OECD membership and comprehensive free trade agreements have eliminated most historical surrender requirements. Capital-account transactions, however, remain subject to a notification and declaration system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations. Foreign direct investment into a Yuhan Hoesa can be settled in KRW or freely convertible foreign currencies after filing a foreign exchange notification through a domestic foreign exchange bank. The key restrictions concern mandatory reporting of large cross-border payments to the Bank of Korea's Foreign Exchange Information System within the prescribed deadline, offshore foreign-currency borrowing requiring a loan report when the borrower is not a licensed financial institution, and profit and dividend remittance, which requires evidence of a valid distribution resolution, payment of Korean tax on those distributable profits, and an underlying foreign-investment notification. The Korean won is convertible for current-account settlements, but speculative capital flows may be moderated through macro-prudential measures, and banks commonly require trade documents before converting large FX amounts into KRW. In practice, permanent profit repatriation hurdles are modest for a low-risk custom keyboard-caps business if all equity injections and shareholder loans are properly reported and annual corporate taxes are paid.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from sales of custom mechanical keyboard caps must be repatriated into a licensed Domestic Foreign Exchange Bank and reported under the Foreign Exchange Information System; the standard statutory collection window is 180 days from the date of export declaration, with a possible extension to one year approved by the bank. No mandatory conversion ratio is imposed in the current liberalised regime; proceeds may be retained in a Foreign Exchange Deposit Account or sold for KRW at the prevailing market rate. An Overseas Foreign Exchange Deposit Account is available only with prior bank authorisation for specific working-capital needs.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for Paid-in Share Capital and Basic Operational KRW Account
Basic Operational Currency Account with Foreign Exchange Deposit Facilities
Export Proceeds Collection Account and Trade Settlement Foreign Currency Account
Currency Account for FX Hedging and Cross-Border Trade Settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a core account substitute. Foreign fintech EMIs and digital payment institutions are not licensed in South Korea under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and cannot hold KRW transactional deposits or provide domestic wire settlement for a Korean corporate entity. They may be used only as payment gateways for international card capture, but settlement of funds into a compliant Korean corporate treasury must occur through a licensed domestic bank. Routing core treasury flows through an offshore EMI would constitute a serious AML red flag and would violate the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-branch onboarding interview is mandatory for the first account opening. At least one authorised signatory who is a Korean-resident director or a locally appointed company officer with a certified board resolution must attend the interview. For non-resident shareholders, a notarised and apostilled Power of Attorney may allow a locally resident representative to complete the interview; pure remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by tier-1 domestic commercial banks. Video-call KYC may supplement but cannot replace the first in-person interview for a non-resident-owned LLC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO with 100% foreign ownership and no Korean tax history; the bank sees potential shell-company structure through nominee-shareholder patterns and sanctions screening hits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Association, current Shareholder Register and UBO Declaration, passport copies and proof of residential address for every natural-person UBO, independent source-of-wealth bank statements, board resolution appointing the Korean resident signatory, tax clearance certificates from each UBO's country of residence, and a negative-media and global sanctions screening report from a reputable independent database.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low nominal paid-in capital with no audited capital-formation trail; a Yuhan Hoesa has no statutory minimum capital, creating concerns about financing of ongoing production.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statement showing the actual capital contribution remitted from the parent or shareholder through a licensed bank with the FDI purpose code, certified capital verification certificate issued by the receiving bank, executed subscriber agreement and board minutes, projected 12-month income statement and cash-flow budget, signed purchase and lease contracts for plastic injection-moulding machinery and warehousing, and supplier agreements with raw-material factories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border e-commerce revenue pattern with frequent small-value credits from Shopify Payments and Stripe, plus refunds and chargebacks, may imply card-laundering or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Live e-commerce store URLs, six months of payment-acquirer settlement reports, export customs declarations, HS classification for keyboard keycaps, carrier bills of lading, warehouse management system order logs, buyer purchase data, an independent draft financial statement, and a reconciliation file linking every chargeback or refund to the original order and the actual merchandise return.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based exposure to suppliers or buyers in jurisdictions with elevated money-laundering risk, or use of third-party consolidation ports in Asia with unclear counterparty ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed KYC file for every supplier and corporate buyer exceeding USD 10,000 in monthly exposure, including business registration certificates, legal representative passports, bank account confirmation letters, Incoterms agreements, export end-user certificates where required, shipment-by-shipment commercial invoices, bill of materials and packing lists, and a licensed third-party logistics consolidation contract with full identity details.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial shareholder capital must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the overseas corporate bank account with the beneficiary clearly identified as the Korean Yuhan Hoesa at the licensed domestic bank. The remitter must state the Foreign Exchange Transaction purpose code for foreign direct equity investment and the company's Foreign Investment Notification reference number. Within the statutory declaration window, the domestic bank files the foreign direct investment acquisition notification with the Ministry of Economy and Finance through the Foreign Exchange Information System. The receiving bank then verifies the paid-in capital against the corporate registration record and issues a Capital Verification Certificate, after which the funds may be released into the operational operating account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for PBT resin, keycap moulds, dyes, packaging and logistics are settled through three compliant clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for standard import invoices with a valid import declaration and FX processing purpose code; Commercial Letters of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700 for large master-order values above USD 100,000 to protect against supplier non-delivery; and Documentary Collections via MT400 for medium-value transactions with trusted repeat suppliers. Every outbound FX purchase must be supported by the underlying trade contract, commercial invoice, packing list, transport document and customs declaration, and must be reported in accordance with Foreign Exchange Transactions Act thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: KRW/USD deliverable forward contracts with a licensed domestic bank for a term matching the export cash-flow cycle, with notional amounts capped at 100% of verified export sales commitments.

FX swaps with an authorised domestic bank for rolling working-capital conversion between the Foreign Exchange Deposit Account and the KRW operating account arising from known trade settlement schedules.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps allowed only where a long-term USD-denominated capital injection or machinery financing loan exists; non-deliverable forward (NDF) structures are not permissible for an onshore Korean entity as a standalone hedging layer because settlement is deliverable in KRW.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None (internal corporate record; minutes and approved financial statements maintained at the registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year; calendar-year entity must hold the meeting by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic administrative strike-off; a member may obtain court authority to convene the meeting, and directors may face administrative fines under the Commercial Act for non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return with annual financial statement attachments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end; calendar-year entity: March 31, with NTS-approved extension available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% non-filing penalty plus daily delinquency interest on unpaid corporate tax; persistent non-payment exposes assets to seizure but does not create administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surtax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (metropolitan city, province, or si/gun/gu tax collection office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the national corporate income tax return; calendar-year entity: March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local surcharge penalties of approximately 3% per month on overdue amounts and enforced collection by the local government; no administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual equalization portion of resident tax for corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (district office in the registered office jurisdiction)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Assessed on July 1 and payable in the July billing cycle, ordinarily by July 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly local tax delinquency surcharge, generally 3% per 30 days, and enforced seizure of bank accounts or assets; failure does not lead to registry strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual wage and salary income withholding aggregate report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 10 following the calendar year of payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing triggers withholding penalties, including up to 50% of the under-withheld amount for intentional under-reporting; continued default may trigger criminal referral but not administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Post-annual-meeting director or representative director registration amendment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean district court commercial registration office having jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks from the date of the relevant change, including annual meeting reappointment or resignation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic administrative strike-off; an unregistered matter cannot be asserted against a bona fide third party, and negligent non-registration is subject to petty fines under the Commercial Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent external audit is mandatory under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, etc. where total assets as of the fiscal year end reach KRW 12 billion (about USD 9 million) or where the company is otherwise designated by the Financial Services Commission; a private LLC below this threshold is exempt from mandatory statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) for listed and large unlisted entities; K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) for non-listed small and medium entities such as the custom mechanical keycap LLC.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea has no public UBO register and no annual UBO declaration for private LLCs. Beneficial ownership is captured through customer due diligence at financial institutions and through the member register maintained by the company under the Commercial Act. Banks and payment acquirers may periodically refresh beneficial ownership data as an internal AML process. Transfers of membership interests must be reflected in the member register; only matters within the commercial registration list, such as appointment of a representative director, are filed at the district court registry.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 12,000 for mandatory audit; below the audit threshold, reviewed financial statements typically cost USD 2,000 - USD 5,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: National Corporate Income Tax rates are progressive: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on income from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on income from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; and 24% on income above KRW 300 billion. A 10% local income tax surcharge on national corporate tax raises the aggregate headline top effective rate to 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket tax holiday is granted to Yuhan Hoesa companies, but targeted incentives apply under the Tax Incentive Limitation Act and Foreign Investment Promotion Act: eligible venture SMEs can benefit from a reduced 10% national rate on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income; R&D expenditure credits up to approximately 30% may be available; job creation, facility investment, strategic industry, and Free Economic Zone incentives can reduce the effective rate for qualifying Korean entities; foreign-invested enterprises may also obtain cash grants or rent/tax exemptions within zones.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return for Domestic Corporation (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Schedule and attached financial statements), filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing system; the related Local Income Tax Return for the 10% local surcharge is filed through the municipal/local tax e-filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return filing; provisional corporate tax installments are required for fiscal years where the prior-year corporate tax liability exceeded KRW 10 million; monthly withholding filings are separately required for salaries, interest, dividends, royalties, and non-resident service fees.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within three months after the end of the fiscal year, by 31 March for a 31 December year-end. A one-month extension is available for overseas accounting or audit reasons, with payment of estimated tax still due by the original statutory deadline; the filed return then is due by 30 April.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Fiscal Year and Entity Identification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates, corporate registration number, trade name, tax office, registered business address, representative director, and shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all non-resident shareholders with foreign country codes and passport numbers; if the Korean LLC has no physical domestic office, identify the in-country responsible agent or tax representative and retain valid board authorization for all Korean filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Net Income per Financial Statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter net income before tax per Korean GAAP or K-IFRS financial statements; this is the reconciliation starting point before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent adjustments have no automatic Korean tax effect; attach standalone Korean financial statements and an intercompany transaction schedule; convert non-KRW amounts into KRW using the base exchange rate announced by the Korean customs authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Non-Deductible Expenses and Add-Back Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back excessive entertainment expenses, non-deductible provisions, depreciation differences, thin capital interest, fines, gifts, and transfer pricing adjustments that have been denied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign related parties require valid invoices, contracts, economic substance, and arm's-length substantiation; head office general and administrative cost allocations are deductible only when properly supported and beneficial to the Korean entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Tax-Exempt Income and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Subtract intercorporate dividend exemptions and other tax-exempt income; deduct eligible Net Operating Loss carryforwards subject to the 10-year limit and taxable income cap of 80% for SMEs or 60% for non-SMEs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a detailed loss carryforward schedule and trace the identity of the legal entity; DTA non-discrimination rules do not grant foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa companies a longer NOL period than domestically owned companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Tax Base, National Tax Computation, and Local Surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the progressive national brackets, compute the 10% local income tax surcharge, then subtract foreign tax credits, R&D credits, employment credits, preliminary tax prepayments, and minimum tax calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits and treaty credits are limited to income effectively connected with the Korean permanent establishment; withholding tax imposed at dividend repatriation cannot be credited against the Korean entity's corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all cross-border related-party transactions, transfer pricing methodology used, arm's-length range, and year-end adjustment positions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A separate annual international transaction statement is mandatory where cross-border related-party transactions aggregate more than KRW 100 million; state the CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, or profit split method applied to each significant intercompany flow.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an additional tax of 20% of the deficient corporate tax; unreasonable or fraudulent underreporting attracts a 40% penalty; ordinary underreporting attracts a 10% penalty; unpaid tax accrues daily interest of approximately 0.025% per day until fully paid; separate administrative fines up to KRW 50 million may apply for failing to file international transaction statements or transfer pricing documentation.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends paid by a Korean Yuhan Hoesa to non-resident shareholders are subject to withholding tax of 20% national income tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge, giving an aggregate statutory withholding rate of 22%, subject to reduction or exemption under an applicable double tax agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must deliver a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the home jurisdiction tax authority to the Korean withholding agent before payment; the withholding agent submits the prescribed DTA relief application through HomeTax with supporting documentation showing beneficial ownership, shareholding percentage, and absence of intermediary/conduit arrangements. The Korean National Tax Service may deny relief where economic substance is absent; if relief is not accepted by the payment date, 22% must be withheld and a refund claim may be filed later within the statutory limitation period, assisted by the DTA Mutual Agreement Procedure when appropriate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Korean withholding on royalty and interest paid to non-residents is also 20% national tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge, aggregating 22%. Under most Korean DTAs, interest withholding ranges from 10% to 15% and royalty withholding generally ranges from 10% to 15%, depending on treaty wording and beneficial ownership; treaty relief requires the same TRC and substance protocol as dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Master File and Local File preparation in Korea is required when aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion (KRW 10,000,000,000); the separate annual international transaction report threshold is KRW 100 million, and taxpayers below the Master File threshold are still expected to retain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation to eliminate or reduce penalties.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the National Tax Service applies the statutory substance-over-form doctrine, the general anti-abuse rule, and DTA beneficial ownership requirements. A Yuhan Hoesa used merely as a booking shell, without genuine board governance, employees, business premises, contracts, accounting records, or operational decision-making in Korea, may be disregarded for tax purposes; treaty benefits are denied, intercompany deductions are disallowed, and the profits are recharacterized as Korean-source income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Unreported Digital Sales
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Shopify or Stripe gross receipts, diverting company sales into the founder's personal PayPal or bank account, generating fake supplier invoices, backdating refunds, or filing a zero revenue return while operating a commercially active mechanical keyboard keycap business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 40% fraudulent understatement penalty on the underpaid corporate tax, daily late-payment interest, seizure of bank and payment processor records, and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to three times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Representative directors and controlling shareholders may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid national and local corporate taxes, penalty surcharges, and interest; the court may issue travel bans, provisional asset seizures, and imprisonment upon conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Related-Party Mispricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling custom keycaps to an overseas affiliate at an artificially deflated resale price, paying excessive royalties to a foreign IP shell, shifting Korean manufacturing profits to an offshore distributor with no employees or premises, or making retroactive year-end TP adjustments unsupported by functional analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: National Tax Service adjustment to the arm's-length consideration, additional tax of up to 40% of the underreported tax, daily delinquency interest, disallowance of royalty or service fee deductions, CFC attribution of deferred foreign income, and separate TP documentation penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign false transfer pricing documentation may be treated as willful tax evaders; they face joint liability for the assessed deficiency, exit bans while the case is pending, criminal referral for tax fraud, and personal liability for related penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominee Korean director, registered agent-only address, no Korean bank account, no employees, no board meetings, no inventory or logistics records, and routing global keyboard cap sales through the Korean entity only to obtain treaty advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service disregards the Korean legal entity form, denies deductions for undocumented expenses, reattributes shifted profit to the Korean taxpayer, imposes the 40% unreasonable claim penalty, cancels treaty benefits, and may cause the company to be administratively struck off for failure of substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts pierce the corporate veil where the entity is an alter ego, making directors jointly liable for corporate taxes and penalties; travel restrictions, seizure of foreign bank accounts, and criminal liability for forged board minutes or invoices may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Profit Repatriation and Withholding Tax Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to non-resident shareholders without withholding 22%, mischaracterizing dividends as loan repayments or expense reimbursements, claiming treaty relief without a TRC or beneficial ownership evidence, or routing payments to indirect foreign shareholders through zero-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of the amount as a taxable dividend, assessment of 22% withholding tax on the gross distribution, under-withholding penalties, daily late-payment interest, denial of treaty relief, and refusal of expense deductions for fictitious intercompany payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director acting as withholding agent is personally liable for unpaid non-resident withholding tax and penalties; willful failure may trigger criminal sanctions, passport cancellation, and collection of foreign assets through international exchange of information.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Foreign Exchange Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring customer receipts to avoid Korean foreign exchange reporting, using unlicensed payment intermediaries, transmitting sales proceeds to a foreign parent or shareholder outside legal banking channels, accepting untraceable cryptocurrency settlements to conceal revenue, or failing to register cross-border capital transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and anti-money laundering laws include administrative fines of up to KRW 100 million, imprisonment of up to 5 years for unlicensed money transmission, forfeiture of laundered proceeds, and revocation of business payment-rail access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who direct or benefit from structured transactions face personal fines, confiscation orders, travel bans, and criminal conviction leading to disqualification from serving as directors of any Korean company.
